title: Reschedule Meetings for Maximum Free Time II
statement:
An event runs from time `0` to time `eventTime`, and `n` meetings happen inside it: meeting `i` occupies `[startTime[i], endTime[i]]`. The meetings are listed in time order and never overlap, although one may end exactly when the next begins.

You may pick at most one meeting and give it a new start time. It keeps its duration, has to stay within `[0, eventTime]`, and must not overlap any other meeting afterwards. It is allowed to jump past other meetings, so the order of the meetings may change.

Return the greatest possible length of a single continuous stretch of the event that no meeting covers.
signature: int maxFreeTime(int eventTime, int[] startTime, int[] endTime)
notes:
## Intuition

Cut the free time into `n + 1` **gaps**: before the first meeting, between neighbours, and after the last. Meeting `i` sits between `gaps[i]` and `gaps[i + 1]`, and moving it can grow the free stretch around it in two ways:

- Slide it against one of its neighbours: its two gaps join, giving `gaps[i] + gaps[i + 1]`.
- Park it inside some **other** gap that is at least as long as the meeting: its own slot frees up as well, giving `gaps[i] + duration + gaps[i + 1]`.

Its own two gaps cannot host it, since they are the free time being grown, so each meeting only needs the largest gap left of `gaps[i]` and the largest right of `gaps[i + 1]`. Trying every meeting at every spot also works, but costs O(n²) or more.

## Approach

1. Build `gaps`: `startTime[0]`, then `startTime[i] - endTime[i - 1]` for each later meeting, then `eventTime - endTime[n - 1]`.
2. Fill `rightMax[g]`, the largest of `gaps[g..n]`, from the right; `rightMax[n + 1] = 0`.
3. Walk the meetings left to right, keeping `leftMax`, the largest of `gaps[0..i - 1]`.
4. For meeting `i`, compute `duration` and `merged = gaps[i] + gaps[i + 1]`. If `leftMax` or `rightMax[i + 2]` is at least `duration`, the candidate is `merged + duration`; otherwise it is `merged`. Keep the largest in `best`.
5. Fold `gaps[i]` into `leftMax` and continue; return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`eventTime = 5`, `startTime = [1, 3]`, `endTime = [2, 5]`, so `gaps = [1, 1, 0]` and `rightMax = [1, 1, 0, 0]`.

- `i = 0`: `duration = 1`, `merged = 2`. `leftMax = 0` and `rightMax[2] = 0`, so no other gap can hold it and `best = 2`. Then `leftMax = 1`.
- `i = 1`: `duration = 2`, `merged = 1`. `leftMax = 1 < 2` and `rightMax[3] = 0`, so the candidate is 1 and `best` stays 2.

The answer is `2`: sliding the first meeting to `[2, 3]` frees `[0, 2]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): building the gaps, the suffix maxima and the final scan are each one pass.
- Space: O(n) for `gaps` and `rightMax`.

## Pitfalls

- The gaps beside meeting `i` cannot host it. For `eventTime = 15`, `startTime = [0, 8, 12]`, `endTime = [3, 11, 15]`, the middle meeting fits in the 5-long gap next to it, yet the answer is 6, not 9.
- A meeting that fits nowhere can still slide, so `merged` alone is always a candidate.
- The border gaps count both as free time and as places to park a meeting.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of meetings |
| `gaps` | the `n + 1` free gaps in time order |
| `rightMax` | `rightMax[g]` is the largest of `gaps[g..n]` |
| `leftMax` | largest gap strictly left of meeting `i`'s own two |
| `duration` | length of meeting `i` |
| `merged` | the two gaps around meeting `i` joined together |
| `best` | longest free stretch found so far |
| `i`, `g` | meeting index and gap index in the loops |

narration.3: The first gap is the free time between the start of the event and the first meeting.
narration.4: Visit every meeting after the first...
narration.5: ...and record the free time between the previous meeting's end and this meeting's start.
narration.7: The last gap is the free time after the final meeting, up to eventTime.
narration.9: rightMax will hold, for each gap index, the largest gap from there to the end; the extra 0 at the end stands for no gap.
narration.10: Fill it from the right so each entry can reuse the one after it.
narration.11: The largest gap from g onward is either gaps[g] itself or the largest from g + 1 onward.
narration.14: leftMax is the largest gap strictly before meeting i's own two gaps; none have been seen yet.
narration.15: best is the longest free stretch found so far.
narration.16: Consider moving each meeting in turn.
narration.17: The meeting keeps this length wherever it goes.
narration.18: Removing the meeting joins the gap before it and the gap after it.
narration.19: Is there a gap away from this meeting, on the left or on the right, long enough to park it in?
narration.20: Yes: park it there, and its own slot becomes free too, so the stretch is both gaps plus its duration.
narration.22: No: the best we can do is slide it against a neighbour, which still merges its two gaps.
narration.24: Before moving right, gaps[i] becomes a gap on the far left of the next meeting.
narration.26: The longest stretch over all choices of meeting is the answer.
